judged_text: In deleteEvent, the same tautological lookup `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined and calendarId falls back to 'primary'. Cancellations delete a (possibly nonexistent) event from the user's primary calendar while the original event in the actual destination calendar is never deleted — orphaned calendar events persist on every cancelled booking that has no externalCalendarId reference.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback calendar selection to:

```ts
externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId
```

This `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` specifically in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, so it will almost always return `undefined` and lose the intended fallback to a destination calendar. In `deleteEvent`, this happens right after `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, so the call will fall back to deleting from `primary` instead of the actual destination calendar when no `externalCalendarId` is provided, leaving the real event undeleted (orphaned). This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff.
